title: Pocket bench compact — run log (Rita Shah)
content:
Purpose: super-compact personal ledger for quick microbench runs. Used while iterating model variants/quant profiles. Keep short, copy relevant rows to full sheet when stable.

How to read: each row = single run (one config, ~30-300 requests). p50/p95 measured on local harness, tokens/sec measured from server logs.

Run table (columns: run_id | model | variant | batch | seq | quant | p50_ms | p95_ms | tok/s | cost_est | notes)

R1  | llama-13b | baseline | 1 | 512 | fp16   | 78  | 210 | 1200 | $0.012 | cold start, small prefix cache
R2  | llama-13b | q4f16   | 1 | 512 | q4f16  | 82  | 240 | 1100 | $0.009 | slight quality drift on long completions
R3  | llama-13b | q4f16+kv | 2 | 256 | q4f16  | 65  | 150 | 2300 | $0.008 | KV cache warm, batching helps latency
R4  | mixtral-8x | baseline | 4 | 128 | fp16  | 52  | 110 | 4100 | $0.010 | great tok/s at small seq, verify truncation artifacts
R5  | mixtral-8x | int8    | 4 | 128 | int8  | 58  | 125 | 3800 | $0.006 | minor nans observed in stress test, re-run w/ cap
R6  | codebird-7b | opt    | 8 | 64  | q8_0   | 28  | 55  | 8400 | $0.004 | cheap/fast for short completions, eval on unit tests

Quick metrics snapshot:
- median p50 across recent week: 62ms
- median p95 across recent week: 160ms
- tokens/s median: 2500
- approximate cost per 1k tokens (weighted): $0.009

Observations / notes to self:
- q4f16 for 13b looks promising cost-wise but check eval set A for hallucination increase (see quick evals below).
- batching of small seq lengths gives best throughput; CPU->GPU memcpy overhead dominates single-request runs.
- mixtral int8 shows good cost reduction, but flaky on long runs; add sanitize/retry wrapper before rollout.
- keep 3 configs as canaries in hosted: baseline-13b, mixtral-int8, codebird-opt for short tasks.

Mini eval results (ad-hoc runs, copy exact prompts to full eval when flagged):
- R2 vs R1 on evalA (50 prompts): exact-match dropped 4.6 pts, but top-3 answers still ok. Need thresholding rule for safety.
- R5 (mixtral int8) on paraphrase detection: precision down 2.2 pts. Might be quantization artifact.

Action items:
- [ ] Re-run R2 with temperature=0.2 and compare exact-match -> todo by 2024-11-05 (assigned to Maya).
- [ ] Instrument retry wrapper for int8 outputs + auto-fallback if NaN or invalid tokens (owner: Rita).
- [ ] Export stable rows to team sheet and tag JIRA-ML-7421 when we have 3 consistent runs.

Open questions / heuristics to test next sprint:
- How to pick canary set that covers both hallucination and API-level latency regressions? propose 15 prompts: 5 factual, 5 multi-step, 5 safety.
- Is q4f16 amplification predictable by prompt length or by distribution of attention peaks? Quick idea: compute attention-sparsity proxy during a sample run.

Scratch math / cost note: tokens counted from server logs approx = generated + prompt; assume 24 tokens/sec = 1M tokens / 11.5 hours at 1 tok/ms baseline. Use these roughs when estimating burst costs.

Local harness commands (short):
- run single: ./bench/run_one.sh --model llama-13b --variant q4f16 --batch 1 --seq 512 --n 50
- run sweep: ./bench/sweep.sh --spec minisweep.yaml --out pocket-runs/2024-10-15

Linked quick evals (ad-hoc):
- file: /home/rita/mini-evals/2024-10-10-evalA.json (local)
- TODO: upload to team confluence if R2 still shows drift

Notes to future self: keep this sheet tiny and ephemeral. When a config makes it to product, copy rows + raw logs to the canonical bench sheet and mark as final.
